review.note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. No terms have been written for Santali because nobody involved in building this system speaks it, and a machine-drafted crisis lexicon in a language the drafter does not know is worse than no lexicon at all: it looks like coverage and produces silent false negatives, in the one category where a false negative is a death. Santali is registered as a supported language regardless, so that a caller reaching 14566 in Santali is served by a counsellor rather than turned away or quietly handled in Hindi. The C-SSRS is administered unconditionally on every interaction, which is precisely why no lexicon is load-bearing on its own — that safeguard is what makes shipping this file empty defensible rather than negligent. Authoring it requires a Santali-speaking counsellor and is the first task in the language section of evidence/PILOT_PROTOCOL.md.

self_harm.note: Feeds the cssrs/self-harm hard rule directly. Escalates to CRITICAL with no model consulted. False positives here cost a counsellor a few minutes; false negatives can cost a life, so the bar for inclusion is deliberately low.

hopelessness.note: Not on its own a crisis trigger; contributes to the distress signal and prompts the intake agent to administer the C-SSRS earlier in the interaction.

imminent_violence.note: Feeds the imminent-threat hard rule. Present tense and immediacy markers matter more than the violence word itself.

isolation.note: Social boycott under s.3(1)(zc) frequently presents in these words before the complainant names it as a boycott.

coercion.note: Pressure to withdraw a complaint. Directly relevant to witness protection under s.15A(11).
